key_insight: The paper proposes an agentic framework that connects a general-purpose orchestrator with specialized radiology AI tools. Its aim is to combine broad clinical coverage with task-specific precision; the provided abstract is incomplete and does not establish performance gains.
problem_solved: Specialized radiology models cover relatively few findings, while generalist models can hallucinate or produce inaccurate measurements. Existing agentic systems are also restricted to a single imaging modality or body part.
method: Introduce a radiology agentic framework centered on an orchestrator.
Standardize how the orchestrator calls specialized AI tools.
Combine generalist capabilities with narrow-task expertise to support more comprehensive radiology reporting.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the framework suggests a modular way to integrate specialized tools rather than relying on one model for every radiology task. Its reliability and clinical value cannot be assessed from the truncated abstract.
visual_elements: Trade-off diagram: specialized models offer narrow precision; generalist models offer broader coverage with reliability risks.
Hub-and-spoke architecture: an orchestrator connected to specialized radiology AI tools.
Conceptual workflow: imaging input → orchestrator → tool calls → consolidated report.
Scope illustration: single-modality systems contrasted with the goal of broader radiology coverage.
paper_title: Can Agentic Systems Close the Gap in Radiology with Production AI Tools?
paper_authors: Aubin Charley, Julien Khlaut, Charles Corbière, Pierre Manceron, Corentin Dancette
